notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order grouped by theme, not a chronology; surah order is not time order. Only three ayat speak of the people to whom Yunus was sent; the story of Yunus himself is not retold here.

claims.statement_en: The Quran asks why there was no town that believed so that its belief benefitted it, except the people of Yunus.
When they believed, God removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world.
God gave them enjoyment for a while.
Another passage says that God sent him to a hundred thousand or more.
The same passage says that they believed, so God gave them enjoyment for a while.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran says that, apart from the people of Yunus, no town believed so that its belief benefitted it [c1]. When they believed, God removed the punishment of disgrace from them and gave them enjoyment for a while [c2][c3].
chapters.body_md: The Quran asks why there was no town that believed so that its belief benefitted it, except the people of Yunus [c1]. When they believed, God removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world [c2]. God gave them enjoyment for a while [c3]. Another passage says that God sent him to a hundred thousand or more [c4]. The same passage says that they believed, so God gave them enjoyment for a while [c5].
chapters.deep_md:
- The Quran asks why there was no town that believed so that its belief benefitted it, except the people of Yunus (10:98) [c1].
- When they believed, God removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world (10:98) [c2].
- God gave them enjoyment for a while (10:98, 37:148) [c3].
- Another passage says that God sent him to a hundred thousand or more (37:147) [c4].
- The same passage says that they believed, so God gave them enjoyment for a while (37:148) [c5].
chapters.kids_md: The Quran says that the people of Yunus believed [c1][c5]. Because they believed, God took away their punishment and let them enjoy life for a while [c2][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage treats belief that came while a warning was still near as something that benefitted the people of Yunus [c1][c2]. One reading is that the ayat hold up their belief as a case that could have been repeated by other towns [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the town was, when this happened, who the people of Yunus were, or how long the enjoyment lasted; the ayat say a while.
- Not established: the number in 37:147 is stated as a hundred thousand or more by the ayah; the ayah does not say how it was counted, and the draft adds nothing to it.
- Not established: the ayat do not say what led them to believe or what the punishment would have been; they say that it was removed.
- Not established: the pronoun of he in 37:147 is not named in that ayah; the draft reads it as Yunus because 10:98 names the people of Yunus.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about the people of Yunus. None is used in this draft.
Wording a scholar should check first: 37:147 (a hundred thousand or more, and the pronoun), 10:98 (the exception).
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the city and the region of the people of Yunus; none is used.
